conviction_note: The findings sum to -0.8 and the scaled number is -0.4 (p_up 48 x abs 10). The two measurements are close because the evidence offsets. A worse EU crop and a mixed Idaho crop, both since July, put the FY27 guide at risk. Against that, the Q1 bar sits inside a guide that LW has beaten for three quarters, US foodservice peers were solid in Jun-Aug, and put demand is at its 52-week high into a Q1 print. Historically this name has changed its crop-based outlook at the December (Q2) print, not the October one. The fundamental read is a small beat (+1%), but this name sells beats (Apr: beat and raise, -8.9%; Jul: above the top of guide, +0.8%), so the reaction read is near zero.
bar: Q1 FY27 revenue $1.66B and EPS $0.59 (Benzinga Pro consensus via https://potatoes.news/us-lamb-weston-to-report-first-quarter-results-on-october-6-as-analysts-expect-eps-to-fall-to-0-59/, 2026-09-30). This agrees with the company's own Q1 guide of 'net sales flat, adjusted EBITDA down low teens' (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-lamb-weston-tops-q4-2026-estimates-as-volume-rises-93CH-4812068, 2026-07-24) on a Q1 FY26 base of $1.66B sales and $302.2M adj EBITDA (https://investors.lambweston.com/news-releases/news-release-details/lamb-weston-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-results-reaffirms). FY27 guide: sales 0-1% growth, adj EBITDA $1.1-1.2B, EPS $2.95-3.25 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001679273/000167927326000024/a-lwx20260531xexx991fy26v2.htm). The bar is sourced and not capped.
positioning_check: Short interest: FINRA 2026-08-31 settlement, 6,294,922 shares, 4.77 days to cover, ~4.6% of shares (https://equibles.com/stocks/lw/short-interest). Ortex gives 4.7% of free float, borrow 0.48%, availability 2,455% of SI. Not crowded, so no squeeze mechanism. The baseline carries no option chain or skew. Ortex reports a put/call ratio of 2.08, more than 2 SD above its 20-day average of 0.91 and level with its 52-week high, up from <0.63 in mid-September. The options market is paying for downside into the print (https://ortex.news/articles/177222/lamb-weston-heads-into-earnings-with-options-traders-at-peak-caution, ~2026-10-02). JANA (4.9%) and Continental Grain (1.5%) are holders.

findings.finding: The Q1 bar sits inside management's own Q1 guide (sales flat, adj EBITDA down low teens from $302.2M). LW beat consensus by wide margins in Q3 FY26 ($0.72 vs $0.63) and Q4 FY26 ($0.87 vs $0.63). Two US foodservice peers reporting the same Jun-Aug period were solid: General Mills NA Foodservice organic +4% with segment OP +12%, and Conagra Foodservice organic +3.3% (volume +2.5%). Both reaffirmed. A modest Q1 beat is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold or ignored: Q3 FY26 (2026-04-01) beat EPS by $0.09 and raised the FY midpoint, -8.94%. Q4 FY26 (2026-07-24) beat above the top of guide, +0.81%. Q1 FY26 (2025-09-30) beat and reaffirmed, +4.33%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Consensus EPS $0.59 (-20% y/y) already embeds the low-teens EBITDA decline, and JPM's preview says publicly that it expects another beat. If the market were pricing a sizable beat, the stock would not sit at put/call 2.08 after target cuts. The residual is only the size of the beat.
findings.independence: General Mills Q1 FY27 release (https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20260922514660/general-mills-reports-fiscal-2027-first-quarter-results-and-reaffirms-full-year-outlook, 2026-09-22/23) and Conagra Q1 FY27 (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CAG/conagra-brands-reports-first-quarter-076d9rt3pjyp.html, 2026-09-30) are independent of LW's documents. JPM 'still expects a beat' (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-jpmorgan-chase-co-has-lowered-expectations-for-lamb-weston-nyse-lw-stock-price-2026-09-30/).

findings.finding: Europe's 2026 crop has turned from the 'average crop' and 'favorable start' management described on 2026-07-24 into the smallest in decades. EU-4 output is ~20.8 Mt, down ~24% y/y, with yields 7-21% below the 5-year average. Belgian/Dutch free-buy processing potatoes have gone from ~EUR 0-15/t in spring to EUR 200-275/t. Management had also flagged a 'more pronounced reduction in contracted volumes', and the 2026 contracts were set 15-25% lower. The EMEA cost for FY27 Q2-Q4 is therefore above what the July guide assumed ('inflation in all inputs other than raw potatoes'). Net of the offset (a short crop ends the EMEA overcapacity price war that took International EBITDA down 81% in Q4, and competitors Clarebout and Lutosa are cutting shifts), the sign leans negative for the guide and the call tone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance and EMEA lines have moved this stock the most. Dec 2025 (Q2: H2 margins flat to down, EMEA curtailed): -25.94%. Dec 2024 (guide cut): -20.10%. Oct 2025 Q1, guide reaffirmed despite EMEA pressure: +4.33%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Stephens cut its target to $50 on exactly this on 2026-09-28, and the stock is -10.6% over 20 days with puts bid. What is not in the price is how much of LW's EMEA supply is exposed to a free-buy market that has risen ~10x, and whether management quantifies it or leaves FY27 untouched. If that exposure were priced in full, the sell-side mean target would not still sit ~20% above spot.
findings.independence: Free-buy prices from a separate source: https://potatoes.news/eu-potato-market-splits-in-two-as-spot-prices-leave-2026-contracts-behind/ (2026-10-03). ECIU crop loss analysis: https://eciu.net/analysis/reports/potato-harvest. Stephens target cut: https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/stephens-cuts-lamb-weston-stock-price-target-on-europe-concerns-93CH-4919969. This is macro-to-company transmission that the company has not yet confirmed, so it is a proxy and sized accordingly.

findings.finding: North American crop since July: Idaho yields are down up to 20% y/y on drought and heat, with smaller tubers, and Lamb Weston is named as receiving smaller tubers from affected growers. The Columbia Basin is reported as average and on par with 2025. In July management said the NA crop was off to a 'strong start' with contracted acreage modestly higher. The new crop is processed from Q2 onward, so lower recovery from small tubers raises cost. A smaller Idaho crop also trims industry oversupply, which supports the 'LSD price/mix decline' assumption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Crop-driven guide changes have historically come at the December (Q2) print once the crop is in storage (Dec 2024 -20.1%, Dec 2025 -25.9%). At the October print the guide was reaffirmed (Oct 2025 +4.3%).
findings.why_not_priced: The sell-side cuts named Europe, not Idaho, and the Idaho reports are trade press from 2026-09-29 to 10-01. Coverage of the NA crop is thin. Offsetting that, the larger Columbia Basin, LW's core region, is average, so the net cost effect is small.
findings.independence: https://capitalpress.com/2026/09/29/weather-shrinks-2026-idaho-potato-yields-butquality-remains-high/ (2026-09-29) points the same way on Idaho. https://hagadonenewsnetwork.com/news/2026/sep/29/early-potato-harvests-looking-strong-for-2026/ (2026-09-29) says the Columbia Basin is average, which cuts against it and is already netted in the size.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is at peak caution. Put/call is 2.08, level with its 52-week high and >2 SD above average. JPM ($46) and Stephens ($50) cut targets in the week before. The stock is -10.6% over 20 days and -33% from its 52-week high. Short interest is modest at 4.7%. A Q1 print that lands on guide and reaffirms FY27, which is what LW did at the last Q1 (Oct 2025, +4.33%), meets hedged rather than long positioning.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 (2025-09-30), guide reaffirmed after a weak run-in: +4.33%. Q4 FY26 after a strong run-up: +0.81%.
findings.why_not_priced: Defensive positioning is by definition the market's view, and this finding runs against the put demand. It is filed because the puts appear to price a guide cut at Q1. LW's own pattern has been to reaffirm at Q1 and reset at Q2, when the crop is in storage. If the market priced that pattern, put/call would not have tripled since mid-September. Sized small because it bets against the options market.
findings.independence: Analyst target cuts: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-stephens-cuts-lamb-weston-nyse-lw-price-target-to-5000-2026-09-28/ (2026-09-28). The Oct 2025 reaffirm reaction comes from the sealed baseline. The +5.9% bounce on 2026-10-02 (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/lamb-weston-stock-gained-5-88-percent-before-its-q1-report/70228662) shows part of the relief may already have been taken.

findings.finding: US QSR traffic, LW's largest channel, is weak. McDonald's US foot traffic has declined y/y in every complete month since March (Placer.ai): -3.1% in the week of Sept 7 against -2.8% for all QSR, and McDonald's Q2 US comps were +0.8%. That threatens the FY27 'low single-digit volume growth' assumption for North America. LW's share wins (+11% NA volume in Q4) cushion it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume/traffic commentary is not separable in the baseline. Q3 FY26 had volume +7% offset by price/mix -7% and the stock fell 8.9%.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (week of Sept 7 data; exact publication date not shown on page)
findings.why_not_priced: It is public traffic data and is largely priced. The residual is how management frames Q2-to-date volumes on the call. This proxy is contradicted for Jun-Aug by the broader foodservice series (GIS +4% and CAG +3.3% organic), so it is sized below them.
findings.independence: Placer.ai's own Q2 piece: https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/why-chipotle-and-mcdonalds-took-different-paths-in-q2-2026. This is a proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: Edible oil inflation continued: US soybean oil held mid-60s to mid-70s c/lb under record 2026-27 RFS biomass-based diesel mandates. Management had already named edible oils as the main Q1 headwind and built it into the low-teens EBITDA decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable. Edible-oil cost was flagged at the July print, and the stock moved +0.81%.

rejected_candidates.detail: The sealed baseline tape (code-computed from daily bars) gives -10.63% over 20 sessions. The article's causes (a Q2 EPS decline, Barclays/Bernstein/BNP cuts) are the December 2025 events relabelled, so the figure is misdated.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew and only a historical-median scale. The negatives (EU and Idaho crops, QSR traffic) agree with the put demand and the -10.6% run-down and are probably largely priced. The one positive (positioning relief on a Q1 reaffirm) cuts against the puts, so it is sized small and p_up sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 and 6 (the beat lands inside the company's own Q1 guide; this name sells beats): reported-quarter finding cut from +0.8 to +0.4, and p_up nudged toward 50 (47 -> 48).
Rule 5 and 'what worked' (weather/crop reasoning is macro-to-company inference, not a company number): EU crop cut from -1.5 to -1.2 and Idaho crop from -0.8 to -0.5. Both stay filed.

Rule 7 (a sign against strong put demand needs a reason or a smaller size): the positioning-relief finding was cut from +1.5 to +1.0. The reason given is that LW historically reaffirms at Q1 and resets at Q2.
Rule 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a broad series): McDonald's/QSR traffic cut from -0.5 to -0.4 because GIS/CAG foodservice organic growth for the same period points the other way.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): edible-oil finding cut from -0.2 to -0.1.
Rule 7 (short interest before negatives): checked. 4.6-4.7% of float, 4.8 days to cover, not crowded, so no negative was shrunk for squeeze risk.
abs_move_pct left at 10.0, the name's own median. The lessons on understatement argue against shrinking it, and Q1 reaffirm prints have been smaller, so nothing moved it.
